Market Update — Executive Summary

Nvidia had one of the most violent sessions in its history on November 12. The board announced that Jensen Huang resigned as President, CEO and director effective immediately, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO and Harvey C. Jones appointed the company's first-ever Chair. The stock gapped from Tuesday's $173.73 close to a $151.01 open, flushed to $148.80, then rallied 11.7% off the low to close at $166.19, almost exactly on the 50% Fibonacci retracement ($165.14) of the April 2025 → October 2026 advance.

The technical read: a high-volume capitulation candle (≈759M shares on the day, the largest bar of the year) that closed near its high. On its own that does not make a bottom. It is the kind of bar that often marks a short-term washout low. Trend tools on every timeframe remain bearish: price is below the 20, 50 and 200-day averages, the FDTS+MACD system is still on a SELL, and the hourly regression channel still points down. Next week's Q3 FY27 earnings (Nov 17) are the binary catalyst, and options are pricing it with 64.7% implied volatility.

FazDane Bottom Line

Bounce, not yet a reversal. $146–$149 is the line in the sand. $172.8 (value-area low) and $183.8–$187.5 (Fib 38.2% + volume POC) are where the bounce gets tested. The probability cone gives a ±1σ range of $150–$184 into Nov 20 and $136–$204 into Dec 18.

Chart 1 — Long-Term Weekly Structure

Figure 1: NVDA weekly chart (2020–present) with Fibonacci retracement drawn from the April 2025 low ($85.99) to the October 2026 high ($244.29 drawing anchor; $243.37 print). The current week's candle (O 173.07 · H 179.92 · L 148.80 · C 166.19) has a long lower wick that pierced toward the 61.8% level ($146.46) and closed back above the 50% level ($165.14).

The big picture is still a secular uptrend. Over this period NVDA went from roughly $11 (Oct 2022 low) to $243. The October–November 2026 decline is a deep but textbook retracement of the last leg. Fibonacci traders treat the 50–61.8% "golden pocket" ($146.46–$165.14) as the area where a healthy uptrend should hold if it is going to hold at all. This week's wick tagged the bottom of that pocket on the worst possible headline and was bought. That is the strongest bullish evidence on the chart.

The dashed red line from the April 2025 low to the highs was the advance's trendline. It broke decisively in late October, so the trend from the 2025 low is broken. Any recovery from here is a new structure, not a continuation of the old one.

Chart 2 — 5-Year Weekly with Volume

Figure 2: NVDA 5-year weekly chart (percent scale) with volume overlay. The current week printed ≈2.0B shares, the heaviest weekly volume since the April 2025 bottom. Fib levels 38.2% $183.82 · 50% $165.14 · 61.8% $146.46.

Volume confirms the significance of the move. The ≈2.0 billion shares traded this week dwarf every week of the 2026 advance. The last comparable spike came at the April 2025 low, which became the launch point for a +181% rally. A volume climax at support is consistent with capitulation, with forced and emotional selling absorbed by larger buyers. Whether it was a true climax only becomes clear if the next retest happens on lighter volume.

Chart 3 — 1-Year Daily Volume Profile

Figure 3: NVDA 1-year daily chart with a volume-at-price profile. Point of control (POC) $187.45 (red), value area $172.82–$214.47 (yellow). Nov 12 bar: O 151.01 · H 167.14 · L 148.80 · C 166.19, volume ≈758.6M.

This is the most actionable chart in the set. The profile shows:

  • Thin air below $172.82: the profile is nearly empty between the value-area low ($172.82) and ~$150. Little trading history means little natural support, which is why the gap went straight to $148.80. It also means a reclaim can travel fast in the other direction.
  • $172.82 is the first real test: regaining and holding the value area would mean the market has accepted the breakdown as a false move. Failing there turns it into resistance.
  • $187.45 POC is the magnet and the ceiling: it is the most-traded price of the year and sits on top of the Fib 38.2% ($183.82), forming a $183.8–$187.5 confluence resistance. Holders who bought there are now underwater and may sell into strength.
  • Reversal-candle anatomy: after a 13% gap down, the bar closed +10.1% above its open and in the top 6% of its range. That is a bullish "hammer" on climax volume. The confirmation needed is a follow-through close above $167.14 (Thursday's high).

The "$157–$160" higher-low zone is the channel's lower deviation of $157.33. The $148.80 low is confirmed by every chart (it is also the Darvas floor). Probability Cone — Where Price Can Go

Figure 5: NVDA probability cone from the $166.19 close through Mar 19, 2027. It uses the 64.7% implied volatility shown on the hourly chart, a lognormal distribution and zero drift. Teal = ±1σ (~68%), blue = ±2σ (~95%), gold dashed = ±1σ if IV drops to 45% after earnings. Horizontal lines are the chart levels identified above.

The cone translates current option pricing into price ranges. The method is the standard one: range = $166.19 × e±kσ√t, with σ = 64.7% and t in trading years. Reading the Cone Correctly

The cone is symmetric in log terms: it has no view on direction. Its key message is width. At 64.7% IV, one standard deviation by Dec 18 is about ±$34. The ~60% touch-odds for $146.46 say that, even if the low holds, a retest is the base case. That is how the support gets proven. Implied volatility normally drops after earnings; the gold dashed lines show the cone narrowing to roughly $144–$192 by Dec 18 if IV resets to 45%. Fat tails and new leadership headlines can push price outside any of these bands.

Fundamental Backdrop — What Changed

  • Leadership shock (confirmed): The Nov 12 8-K and press release confirm Huang's resignation, Kress as interim CEO while she stays CFO, and Jones as Chair. The board says operations, customer commitments and the roadmap continue without interruption, and it is searching internal and external candidates for a permanent CEO.
  • Allegations (unresolved): Press reports tie the departure to a personal relationship and alleged foreign-intelligence links. These are allegations, not findings. China has called the spy claim a smear. The market is pricing key-person and governance risk, not an operating collapse.
  • Earnings Nov 17: per the research note, Q2 FY27 revenue was $96.2B (Data Center $89.0B, 75.0% GM), with Q3 guidance of $108.0B ±2% and ~74% GM. Guidance continuity plus Kress's credibility as the long-time CFO is the most likely stabilizing catalyst. Any wobble in guidance would turn a valuation discount into an earnings problem.
  • Structural headwinds (longer-term): custom silicon (Google TPU, Microsoft Maia, AWS Trainium) and gains in model efficiency threaten growth rate and margins more than absolute demand. Revenue grew ~43× from FY2016 to FY2026, and repeating that is not the base case.

Summary & Actionable Conclusions
Event Shock

CEO resignation triggered a 13% gap and a $148.80 flush, a governance repricing, not yet evidence of an operating collapse.

Capitulation Signature

Year-high volume, hammer close +10% off the open, WRP < −80 with buy dots: the anatomy of a washout low.

Ceiling Overhead

$172.82 value-area low, then $183.8–$187.5 (Fib 38.2% + POC). Trend tools stay bearish below there.

Cone Ranges

±1σ: $150–$184 by Nov 20 · $136–$204 by Dec 18. ~60% odds of touching $146.46 again by Dec 18.

Do Not Chase

Earnings in 3 sessions with 64.7% IV. Let the retest prove the low and buy a higher low, not a gap.

Bias & Plan

Neutral-to-constructive above $146.46; bearish below. Swing long on a $152–$158 higher low, stop < $146, target $184–$187.
